practiceQuestions.q: Under which Article of the Indian Constitution is the Legislative Assembly (Vidhan Sabha) established?
practiceQuestions.sol: Article 170 of the Indian Constitution deals with the composition of the Legislative Assemblies. Article 168 deals with the constitution of legislatures in states, Article 171 deals with the Legislative Council, and Article 172 deals with the duration of state legislatures.

practiceQuestions.q: What is the maximum permissible strength of a State Legislative Assembly as per the Constitution of India?
practiceQuestions.sol: According to Article 170, the Legislative Assembly of a state shall consist of not more than 500 and not less than 60 members chosen by direct election from territorial constituencies in the state.

practiceQuestions.q: What is the minimum permissible strength of a State Legislative Assembly under the Constitution, subject to specific exceptions?
practiceQuestions.sol: Article 170 prescribes a minimum limit of 60 members for a Legislative Assembly. However, exceptions exist for smaller states like Sikkim, Mizoram, and Goa where the strength is lower than 60 by special constitutional provisions.

practiceQuestions.q: Which constitutional amendment abolished the provision of nomination of an Anglo-Indian member to the State Legislative Assemblies?
practiceQuestions.sol: The 104th Constitutional Amendment Act, 2019, ceased the nomination of Anglo-Indian members to the Lok Sabha and State Legislative Assemblies, as their population no longer warranted special representation.

practiceQuestions.q: What is the normal tenure of a State Legislative Assembly from the date appointed for its first meeting?
opts: It is a permanent body not subject to dissolution
practiceQuestions.sol: Under Article 172, every Legislative Assembly of every State, unless sooner dissolved, continues for five years from the date appointed for its first meeting and no longer.

practiceQuestions.q: What is the minimum age required for a person to contest elections to the State Legislative Assembly?
practiceQuestions.sol: According to Article 173(b), a person must be not less than 25 years of age to be qualified to fill a seat in the Legislative Assembly (similar to the Lok Sabha).

practiceQuestions.q: Who has the authority to dissolve the State Legislative Assembly before the completion of its normal 5-year term?
opts: Governor on the aid and advice of the Chief Minister
President of India on the recommendation of the Governor
Chief Justice of the State High Court
practiceQuestions.sol: The Governor can dissolve the Legislative Assembly at any time on the recommendation of the Chief Minister (representing the Council of Ministers), as per Article 174(2)(b).

practiceQuestions.q: What is the quorum required to constitute a meeting of the State Legislative Assembly?
opts: One-tenth of the total number of members of the House
practiceQuestions.sol: Under Article 189(3), the quorum to constitute a meeting of a House of the State Legislature is ten members or one-tenth of the total number of members of the House, whichever is greater.

practiceQuestions.q: Which of the following states has the largest Legislative Assembly in terms of member strength?
practiceQuestions.sol: Uttar Pradesh has the largest Legislative Assembly in India with 403 elected members, owing to its high population size.

practiceQuestions.q: During a proclamation of National Emergency, for what maximum period can the Parliament extend the normal tenure of a State Legislative Assembly at a time?
opts: Until the emergency is completely revoked
practiceQuestions.sol: Under the proviso to Article 172(1), when a proclamation of National Emergency is in operation, the Parliament may by law extend the life of a Legislative Assembly for a period not exceeding one year at a time and not extending in any case beyond a period of six months after the Proclamation has ceased to operate.

practiceQuestions.q: Why does the Indian Constitution grant pre-eminence to the Legislative Assembly over the Legislative Council in legislative matters?
opts: Because the Legislative Assembly is directly elected by the people embodying democratic legitimacy.
Because the Legislative Council is a permanent body that cannot be dissolved.
Because the Governor is a member of the Legislative Assembly.
Because the Supreme Court mandated bicameral supremacy for Assemblies.
practiceQuestions.sol: The Legislative Assembly is directly elected by the electorate, representing the principle of popular sovereignty and democratic mandate. The Legislative Council is an advisory, revising chamber with limited powers, reflecting the design of the framers to avoid deadlocks while prioritizing democratic will.

practiceQuestions.q: How does the financial power of the State Legislative Assembly structurally differ from that of the Legislative Council?
opts: Money Bills can originate in either house of the state legislature with mutual consent.
Money Bills can only be introduced in the Legislative Assembly, and the Legislative Council has a maximum delaying power of 14 days.
The Legislative Council can reject a Money Bill passed by the Legislative Assembly permanently.
Both houses have equal voting powers on the demands for grants.
practiceQuestions.sol: Under Article 198, Money Bills can be introduced only in the Legislative Assembly. The Legislative Council cannot reject or amend a Money Bill; it can only make recommendations within 14 days, which the Assembly may accept or reject.

practiceQuestions.q: What happens to ordinary bills pending in the Legislative Assembly when the Assembly is dissolved?
opts: They are automatically transferred to the Legislative Council for enactment.
They remain pending until the next newly elected Assembly is constituted.
They are promulgated as ordinances by the Governor.
practiceQuestions.sol: According to Article 196, a bill pending in the Legislative Assembly lapses upon its dissolution, regardless of whether it originated in the Assembly or was transmitted from the Legislative Council.

practiceQuestions.q: In the event of a deadlock between the two Houses of a bicameral State Legislature over an ordinary bill, what is the constitutional mechanism provided?
opts: A joint sitting of both Houses summoned by the Governor.
No provision for a joint sitting; the Legislative Assembly's will ultimately prevails.
Referendum conducted by the Election Commission of India.
Arbitration by the Supreme Court of India.
practiceQuestions.sol: Unlike Parliament, the Constitution of India does *not* provide for a joint sitting of the two Houses of a state legislature. The Legislative Assembly enjoys ultimate overriding power; if the Council rejects a bill or passes it with unacceptable amendments, the Assembly can pass it a second time and send it to the Council, which can only delay it further.

practiceQuestions.q: What is the significance of the Speaker's casting vote under Article 189 of the Constitution?
opts: It allows the Speaker to vote in the first instance on any motion.
It can be exercised only to resolve a tie, ensuring legislative business is not deadlocked.
It gives the Speaker veto power over bills passed by the Assembly.
It allows the Speaker to override the Governor's assent.
practiceQuestions.sol: Under Article 189(1), the Speaker does not vote in the first instance. The casting vote is used exclusively when there is an equality of votes on either side, maintaining neutrality while breaking a tie.

practiceQuestions.q: How does the Delimitation Commission affect the composition of the State Legislative Assembly?
opts: It alters the total number of seats in the Assembly at every census.
It readjusts territorial constituencies and reservation of seats for SCs and STs based on the latest census population data.
It determines the political party affiliations of candidates.
It fixes the salaries and allowances of the MLAs.

practiceQuestions.sol: Under Article 170, upon the completion of each census, the allocation of seats in the Legislative Assembly to the states and the division of each state into territorial constituencies is readjusted by such authority and in such manner as Parliament may determine via Delimitation Commission Acts.

practiceQuestions.q: What is the unique constitutional position regarding the Speaker of the Legislative Assembly upon dissolution of the House?
opts: The Speaker immediately vacates office as soon as the Assembly is dissolved.
The Speaker continues in office until immediately before the first meeting of the newly elected Assembly.
The Speaker assumes the role of acting Governor during the interregnum.
The Speaker is automatically appointed as the Pro-Tem Speaker.
practiceQuestions.sol: Unlike the Lok Sabha Speaker, who vacates office immediately before the first meeting of the newly elected house, the provision for state legislatures under Article 179 states that the Speaker does *not* vacate office upon dissolution and continues until immediately before the first meeting of the new Assembly.

practiceQuestions.q: Why are seats reserved for Scheduled Castes (SCs) and Scheduled Tribes (STs) in the State Legislative Assembly?
opts: To ensure adequate political representation proportional to their population share, fulfilling constitutional egalitarian objectives.
To permanently prevent general category candidates from contesting elections.
To comply with international human rights treaties.
To exempt them from paying municipal taxes in the state.

practiceQuestions.sol: Article 332 mandates the reservation of seats for SCs and STs in the Legislative Assembly of every state, proportionate to their respective population, to safeguard their political voice and integrate marginalized communities into the democratic framework.

practiceQuestions.q: What is the primary constitutional role of a 'Pro-Tem Speaker' appointed in the State Legislative Assembly?
opts: To preside over the permanent legislative business of the new Assembly for its full term.
To administer oaths to newly elected MLAs and preside over the election of the permanent Speaker.
To act as the Leader of the Opposition when no majority party exists.
To advise the Governor on the dissolution of the Council of Ministers.

practiceQuestions.sol: The Pro-Tem Speaker is a temporary officer appointed by the Governor specifically to administer oaths to new members and conduct the election of the regular Speaker. Once the regular Speaker is elected, the office of the Pro-Tem Speaker ceases to exist.

practiceQuestions.q: How does the power of the State Legislative Assembly over the state budget (annual financial statement) compare with executive dominance?
opts: The budget is finalized by the cabinet without requiring assembly voting.
No demand for a grant can be made except on the recommendation of the Governor, but the Assembly has the ultimate power to assent, reduce, or refuse any grant.
The Legislative Assembly can increase taxes without executive concurrence.
The executive can spend money from the Consolidated Fund without legislative authorization.

practiceQuestions.sol: Under Article 203, estimates of expenditures are submitted as demands for grants to the Legislative Assembly. While grants require the Governor's recommendation (reflecting executive initiative), the Assembly holds the absolute authority to assent or refuse assent to any demand, or to reduce its amount, establishing legislative financial control.

practiceQuestions.q:
Consider the following statements regarding the State Legislative Assembly:
1. The Constitution fixes both the maximum and minimum limits for the strength of a State Legislative Assembly.
2. All members of the Legislative Assembly are directly elected by the people from territorial constituencies.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
practiceQuestions.sol: Statement 1 is correct: Article 170 specifies a maximum of 500 and a minimum of 60 members. Statement 2 is correct: Under Article 170(1), the Assembly consists of members chosen by direct election from territorial constituencies (with the Anglo-Indian nomination now abolished via the 104th Amendment). Thus, both statements are correct.

practiceQuestions.q:
Consider the following statements regarding the duration and dissolution of the Legislative Assembly:
1. The normal tenure of the Legislative Assembly is 5 years, and it cannot be dissolved before this period under any circumstances.
2. During a National Emergency, Parliament can extend the life of a Legislative Assembly for a maximum period of one year at a time.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
practiceQuestions.sol: Statement 1 is incorrect because the Governor can dissolve the Assembly earlier on the advice of the Chief Minister. Statement 2 is correct: Under Article 172(1) proviso, Parliament can extend the Assembly's tenure by up to one year at a time during a National Emergency.

practiceQuestions.q:
Consider the following statements regarding the qualifications for membership of the Legislative Assembly:
1. A person must be not less than 30 years of age to contest election to the Legislative Assembly.
2. The candidate must be an elector for any parliamentary or legislative constituency in the state.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
practiceQuestions.sol: Statement 1 is incorrect because the minimum age for the Legislative Assembly is 25 years (30 years is for the Legislative Council). Statement 2 is correct: Representation of the People Act, 1951 requires a candidate contesting for the Assembly to be an elector for any assembly constituency in that state.

practiceQuestions.q:
Consider the following statements regarding Money Bills in State Legislatures:
1. A Money Bill can be introduced in either the Legislative Assembly or the Legislative Council.
2. The Legislative Council has the power to amend or reject a Money Bill passed by the Legislative Assembly.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
practiceQuestions.sol: Both statements are incorrect. Statement 1 is wrong because a Money Bill can only be introduced in the Legislative Assembly, not the Council. Statement 2 is wrong because the Council cannot amend or reject a Money Bill; it can only make recommendations within 14 days.

practiceQuestions.q:
Consider the following statements regarding the Speaker of the Legislative Assembly:
1. The Speaker is elected by the Legislative Assembly from amongst its members.
2. Upon dissolution of the Legislative Assembly, the Speaker vacates office immediately.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
practiceQuestions.sol: Statement 1 is correct: Article 178 mandates that the Assembly shall choose two members to be Speaker and Deputy Speaker respectively. Statement 2 is incorrect: Under Article 179, the Speaker does not vacate office upon dissolution and remains in office until immediately before the first meeting of the new Assembly.

practiceQuestions.q:
Consider the following statements regarding ordinary bills originating in the Legislative Assembly:
1. If a bill is passed by the Legislative Assembly and transmitted to the Legislative Council, the Council can delay it for a maximum period of 4 months in total.
2. There is a provision for a joint sitting of both houses of the state legislature to resolve a deadlock over an ordinary bill.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
practiceQuestions.sol: Statement 1 is correct: The Legislative Council can delay an ordinary bill for 3 months on the first instance and 1 month on the second transmission, totaling 4 months. Statement 2 is incorrect because the Constitution provides *no* mechanism for a joint sitting of state legislature houses.

practiceQuestions.q:
Consider the following statements regarding the powers and position of the Legislative Assembly:
1. The Council of Ministers in the state is collectively responsible to the Legislative Assembly.
2. A motion of no-confidence against the government can be introduced in the Legislative Council.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
practiceQuestions.sol: Wait, let's check options carefully. Statement 1 is correct: Article 164(2) states that the Council of Ministers shall be collectively responsible to the Legislative Assembly. Statement 2 is incorrect: A no-confidence motion can only be introduced in the Legislative Assembly, not the Legislative Council. Therefore, 1 only is correct.

practiceQuestions.q:
Consider the following statements regarding the voting and quorum in the Legislative Assembly:
1. All questions at any sitting of the Legislative Assembly shall be determined by a majority of votes of the members present and voting, other than the Speaker or person acting as such.
2. The quorum to constitute a meeting of the Legislative Assembly is fixed at one-third of the total members of the House.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
practiceQuestions.sol: Statement 1 is correct under Article 189(1). Statement 2 is incorrect because the quorum is one-tenth of the total number of members of the House (or 10 members, whichever is greater), not one-third.

practiceQuestions.q:
Consider the following statements regarding constitutional amendment bills and the State Legislative Assembly:
1. State Legislative Assemblies have the power to initiate constitutional amendment bills under Article 368.
2. Certain constitutional amendment bills passed by Parliament require ratification by not less than half of the State Legislative Assemblies.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
practiceQuestions.sol: Statement 1 is incorrect because state legislatures cannot initiate constitutional amendment bills; such bills can only be introduced in either House of Parliament. Statement 2 is correct under Article 368(2) proviso, where federal provisions require ratification by at least half of the state legislatures.

practiceQuestions.q:
Consider the following statements regarding the disqualification of members of the State Legislative Assembly:
1. The Constitution sets out explicit grounds for disqualification including holding an office of profit and being of unsound mind.
2. The decision on whether a member has incurred disqualification under the Tenth Schedule (Anti-Defection Law) rests with the Governor of the state.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
practiceQuestions.sol: Statement 1 is correct: Article 191 specifies grounds for disqualification (office of profit, unsound mind, undischarged insolvent, etc.). Statement 2 is incorrect: Under the Tenth Schedule, the question of disqualification on grounds of defection is decided by the Speaker (or Chairman) of the House, *not* the Governor (though general disqualifications under Art 191 are decided by the Governor in consultation with the Election Commission).
